naviguer-dans-le-dashboard.title: Navigate the dashboard
naviguer-dans-le-dashboard.summary: Key landmarks: sidebar, breadcrumbs, notifications, and quick help access.
naviguer-dans-le-dashboard.body:
After you sign in, the [dashboard](/dashboard) shows KPIs and recent activity. The left sidebar groups modules: users, products, bookings, payments, content, GAP, and system.

The breadcrumb at the top of the page shows where you are and lets you move up one level. On mobile, open the menu with the hamburger icon. The bell icon opens the [notification center](/notifications) without leaving the current page.

Use the [Help Center](/aide) or admin search (magnifier icon, Ctrl+F) to reach a page, a help article, or a business record quickly without scanning the whole menu. On every screen, the Help icon in the header opens the recommended article for the current module.

Tip: start with Quick start on /aide (users, bookings, roles, tickets) to learn the daily actions before exploring advanced topics.

notifications.title: Notification center
notifications.summary: View, filter, and process admin alerts.
notifications.body:
Open Notifications in the menu (or the bell icon) to reach the [notification center](/notifications). You will find alerts related to bookings, messages, support tickets, and other events.

Filter by type or status to focus on what still needs action. Mark items as read after you handle them to keep the inbox clear.

Badges in the navigation (pending reviews, open tickets) link to the relevant modules.

palette-commandes.title: Admin search (Ctrl+F)
palette-commandes.summary: Search pages, help, and business data via the magnifier or Ctrl+F (command palette).
palette-commandes.body:
Open admin search with the header magnifier icon, or the shortcuts Ctrl+F / Cmd+F (alias Ctrl+K / Cmd+K). Type to filter menu pages and help articles first, then — from two characters — business records according to your permissions: users and employees, organizations, bookings, properties, payments, [promotions](/paiements/promotions) and [promo codes](/paiements/codes-promo), support tickets, catalog (activities, flights, vehicles, packages, cruises, destinations), [tour guides](/guides), blog, GAP pages and activities, and [roles](/systeme/roles).

Results arrive in waves (pages/help first, then core business data, then catalog) and deep-link straight to the matching record. Navigate with ↑↓ and press Enter to open. Results are grouped (Pages, Help, Users, Payments…). Close with Escape or the same shortcut.

While typing in a form field, Ctrl+F keeps the browser’s native find; outside a field, it opens admin search. Press ? for keyboard-shortcut help (including Ctrl+L to lock the session), then follow the link to the [Help Center](/aide) if needed.

Combine the magnifier / Ctrl+F with the header Help icon: the first jumps to a page or record, the second opens docs for the module you are on.

raccourcis-clavier.title: Keyboard shortcuts
raccourcis-clavier.summary: Open help with ?; search with Ctrl+F; lock with Ctrl+L.
raccourcis-clavier.body:
Press the ? key (when you are not typing in a field) to open the keyboard shortcuts panel. It lists combinations available in the admin shell.

The main shortcut is Ctrl+F / Cmd+F for admin search (pages, help, and business data). Ctrl+K / Cmd+K remains an alias. Escape closes search or this help panel.

Ctrl+L / Cmd+L locks your admin session immediately (including when focus is in a field). The lock screen asks for your password to continue, or lets you sign out. The same lock can also trigger after a period of inactivity — see [Sessions and security logs](/aide/utilisateurs-acces/sessions-et-securite).

If a shortcut does nothing, check that you are signed in to the dashboard (not on the login page). Outside a text field, Ctrl+F opens admin search instead of the browser’s native find.

gerer-les-utilisateurs.title: Manage users
gerer-les-utilisateurs.summary: Create, search, and update accounts — the foundation of platform access.
gerer-les-utilisateurs.body:
The [Users](/utilisateurs) module lists customer and staff accounts on the platform. Filter by status or organization, then open a record to view or edit the profile.

To create an account, use New user. Fill in the required fields and save. Depending on your permissions (users.read / users.write), some actions may be hidden.

From the record you can review details, link an employee profile, or go to [sessions](/utilisateurs/sessions) and [security logs](/utilisateurs/journaux-securite) for access auditing. [Roles and permissions](/systeme/roles) then control what that account can open in the admin.

If a customer reports an account issue, cross-check [Support](/contenu/support) and review active [sessions](/utilisateurs/sessions) before resetting access.

employes-et-departements.title: Employees and departments
employes-et-departements.summary: Link users to organizations and structure teams.
employes-et-departements.body:
[Employees](/utilisateurs/employes) associate a user with an organization and a department. Create an employee from an existing user account, then enter the code, job title, and assignment.

[Departments](/utilisateurs/departements) classify staff (sales, support, operations, and so on). They are used as a reference when creating or editing an employee.

These screens usually require employees.read / departments.read (and the matching write permissions to edit).

sessions-et-securite.title: Sessions and security logs
sessions-et-securite.summary: Screen lock, active logins, and access auditing.
sessions-et-securite.body:
Two security layers coexist in the admin.

Workstation lock: after a period of inactivity (often about 60 minutes), or immediately via Ctrl+L / Cmd+L, the interface locks. Enter your password to resume, or sign out. Shortcut details are in [Keyboard shortcuts](/aide/prise-en-main/raccourcis-clavier).

User sessions (multi-device): in [Sessions](/utilisateurs/sessions), review users’ active sessions. You can revoke a session to force a sign-out (lost device, suspicious access).

[Security logs](/utilisateurs/journaux-securite) record authentication and audit events. Use them to investigate an incident or verify recent activity.

These tools complement [roles and permissions](/systeme/roles): a revoked session grants no access even if the account remains active.

adresses-et-moyens-paiement.title: Addresses and payment methods
adresses-et-moyens-paiement.summary: View addresses and cards saved by users.
adresses-et-moyens-paiement.body:
The [Addresses](/utilisateurs/adresses) module shows addresses saved by users (billing, delivery, travel). Filter or search to find an entry linked to an account.

[Payment methods](/utilisateurs/moyens-paiement) list cards and other methods saved by users. This data is for support and follow-up; booking payments are handled in the [Payments](/paiements) module.

Respect privacy: export or share this information only within your role and permissions.

hebergements.title: Manage accommodations
hebergements.body:
The [Accommodations](/hebergements) module lists properties (hotels, lodges, and so on). Filter by destination, search by name, then open a record to edit or view details.

Create a property with New accommodation, then add images, amenities, rooms, and availability from the edit page. Global amenities are managed in the related catalog.

Access is controlled by properties.read / properties.write. A complete property record improves bookings and the public site listing.

vols-locations-croisieres.title: Flights, rentals, and cruises
vols-locations-croisieres.summary: Air catalog, vehicles, and cruise sailings.
vols-locations-croisieres.body:
Under Products there are three verticals: [Flights](/produits/vols), [Rentals](/produits/locations), and [Cruises](/produits/croisieres).

For flights, manage airlines, airports, and offers; for rentals, agencies, categories, and vehicles with slots; for cruises, ships, lines, ports, and sailings.

Use the “New…” screens and nested pages (ships, ports, agencies…) from the module or admin search (Ctrl+F). Each vertical has its own permissions (flights, vehicles, cruises).

activites-et-forfaits.title: Activities and packages
activites-et-forfaits.summary: Experiences, partners, time slots, and combined packages.
activites-et-forfaits.body:
[Activities](/produits/activites) describe the experiences on offer. Create an activity, attach a destination and partner, then add slots or options on the edit page.

[Packages](/produits/forfaits) combine several products (accommodation, activity, and so on) into one packaged offer. Build the package contents, then publish according to your workflow.

When no slots remain, [booking requests](/produits/activites/demandes) collect customer inquiries (if the option is enabled on the activity).

Typical permissions: activities.read/write and packages.read/write. Check destinations and pricing before going live.

demandes-reservation-activites.title: Activity booking requests
demandes-reservation-activites.summary: Handle customer inquiries with no slots: status, email, and adding a slot.
demandes-reservation-activites.body:
The [Booking requests](/produits/activites/demandes) page lists inquiries submitted from the public site when an [activity](/produits/activites) has no remaining slots and “Allow booking requests when no slots” is enabled on the activity form.

These are not confirmed [bookings](/reservations): no payment has been taken. Filter by activity, status, or search (name / email), then change the status (pending, contacted, confirmed, cancelled). Before you confirm, a preview of the customer email is shown — it clearly states whether a slot is now available or the activity remains unavailable.

From the Actions column, open the modal to [add a time slot](/produits/activites) (datetime and capacity prefilled from the request). A [notification](/notifications) is also created for each new inquiry.

Permission activities.read to view the list and activities.write to update status or create a slot.

destinations.title: Destinations
destinations.summary: Geography, points of interest, and product linking.
destinations.body:
[Destinations](/produits/destinations) structure the platform geography (countries, regions, places). Search by name, slug, or country code.

Create a destination, then enrich it with points of interest and map coordinates. Many products (accommodations, activities, and so on) link to it.

Permission destinations.read / destinations.write. Clear destinations improve public search and admin filtering.

gerer-les-reservations.title: Manage bookings
gerer-les-reservations.summary: Track requests, travelers, statuses, and related payments in one place.
gerer-les-reservations.body:
The [Bookings](/reservations) module centralizes customer bookings. Filter by status, dates, or reference, then open the detail to see lines, travelers, documents, and history.

Depending on status, you can advance processing, review payment proofs, or coordinate with support. Permissions bookings.read / bookings.write apply.

For a payment issue or customer incident, cross-check [Payments](/paiements) and [Support](/contenu/support). Assign a guide via the [guides](/guides) calendar when the product requires it.

Breadcrumbs, admin search (Ctrl+F), and the header Help icon let you switch quickly between booking, payment, and ticket without losing context.

guides-et-calendrier.title: Tour guides and calendar
guides-et-calendrier.body:
The [Guides](/guides) module manages tour guide profiles. Create a guide, fill in the bio and useful details, then track their availability calendar.

Use planning views to avoid assignment conflicts and align guides with related bookings or activities.

Permission guides.read / guides.write. A complete guide profile helps field operations and booking follow-up.

suivre-les-paiements.title: Track payments
suivre-les-paiements.summary: Statuses, amounts, and links to bookings.
suivre-les-paiements.body:
The [Payments](/paiements) module lists transactions tied to bookings and other collections. Filter by status, method, or period to find a payment.

Open the detail to see amount, reference, method (card, mobile money, offline…), and any link to the booking. Watch failures and payments pending validation.

Permission payments.read (and write for some actions). For a customer dispute, cross-check [Bookings](/reservations) and support tickets.

codes-promo.title: Promo codes
codes-promo.summary: Create, limit, and monitor discount codes.
codes-promo.body:
[Promo codes](/paiements/codes-promo) apply a discount at checkout. Create a code with New promo code: set the type (percentage or amount), validity, usage caps, and conditions.

Monitor usage from the list or the detail page. Disable a code as soon as a campaign ends to prevent abuse.

Permission promo_codes.read / promo_codes.write. Test the code on a booking flow before a large campaign.

promotions.title: Promotions
promotions.summary: Promotional campaigns shown or applied to offers.
promotions.body:
[Promotions](/paiements/promotions) cover campaigns broader than a single code (featured offers, seasonal deals, and so on). Create a promotion, set dates and scope, then save.

Distinguish promotions (campaign / showcase) from promo codes (customer enters a code). Both can run in the same period.

Permission promotions.read / promotions.write. Align the promo calendar with stock and pricing for the products involved.

parametres-gap.title: GAP settings
parametres-gap.summary: Configure the Gorilla Ambassadors Program site.
parametres-gap.body:
GAP (Gorilla Ambassadors) has its own [settings](/gap/parametres). Adjust the GAP site configuration (identity, display options, operational settings as shown on screen).

Change only fields you understand, then save. Check the preview or public GAP site after a sensitive change.

Permission gap.read / gap.write. These settings are separate from general organization [settings](/parametres).

pages-et-activites-gap.title: GAP pages and activities
pages-et-activites-gap.summary: Editorial content and ambassador program activities.
pages-et-activites-gap.body:
[GAP pages](/gap/pages) manage editorial content for the ambassadors site (create, edit, publish). Start with New GAP page, then fill in title, body, and metadata.

[GAP activities](/gap/activites) describe actions or experiences linked to the program. Create and organize them like the main activity catalog, but within the GAP scope.

Stay consistent with the brand guidelines and [GAP settings](/gap/parametres). Permissions gap.read / gap.write.

impact-et-medias-gap.title: GAP impact and media
impact-et-medias-gap.body:
[GAP impact](/gap/impact) presents featured statistics and indicators (donations, results, milestones). Add or update a statistic with New impact statistic.

[GAP media](/gap/medias) centralizes images and files reused in pages and activities. Upload assets with clear names and web-friendly dimensions.

Keep numbers and visuals current: they support the program’s credibility on the public site.

blog-et-site.title: Blog and presentation site
blog-et-site.summary: Blog posts and institutional content (About, hero, team…).
blog-et-site.body:
The [blog](/contenu/blog) lets you create and publish posts for the public site. Use New post, enter localized content, then publish according to your workflow.

Site & [presentation](/contenu/site) groups institutional pages: About, team, timeline, resources, Why us, hero carousel, and happy customers. Use tabs to edit each section.

Permissions blog.read/write and content.read/write. Preview the public site after a major change.

pages-legales.title: Legal pages
pages-legales.summary: Terms, privacy, and other legal texts.
pages-legales.body:
[Legal pages](/contenu/legal) manage legal documents shown on the site (terms, privacy, and so on). Create or update a page with New legal page.

Watch the language version (fr / en / es) and the update date. An outdated page creates compliance risk.

Permission content.read / content.write. Have sensitive texts reviewed before publishing.

moderer-les-avis.title: Moderate customer reviews
moderer-les-avis.summary: Approve, hide, or delete ratings and comments.
moderer-les-avis.body:
The [Reviews](/contenu/avis) module centralizes ratings and comments left by customers. Filter by rating, property, or status (pending, published, hidden).

From the detail view, approve, hide, or delete a review according to your policy. The “pending reviews” badge in the menu shows the moderation backlog.

Permissions reviews.read / reviews.write. Handle flagged reviews quickly to protect reputation and public content quality.

tickets-support-clients.title: Customer support tickets
tickets-support-clients.summary: Work the support queue: priority, reply, status, and closure.
tickets-support-clients.body:
The [Support](/contenu/support) hub manages customer tickets (Tickets tab) and prepares unified messaging (Messages tab). Filter by status and priority, then open a ticket to read the thread and reply.

Assign the ticket, change the status (open → pending → resolved / closed), and send a reply of at least ten characters. The “open tickets” badge in the navigation shows remaining workload.

Permissions support_tickets.read / support_tickets.write. Do not confuse this module with the admin [Help Center](/aide), which is for internal documentation only.

When a ticket relates to a booking or account, open the linked record (Ctrl+F search or contextual Help) to verify status before you reply to the customer.

comptes-fidelite-onekey.title: OneKey loyalty accounts
comptes-fidelite-onekey.summary: Point balances, tiers, and manual adjustments.
comptes-fidelite-onekey.body:
[Loyalty accounts](/fidelite/comptes) show the OneKey program: point balance, tier, and last activity. Search by user to inspect history.

Manual balance adjustments may be limited to the super administrator. Document the reason for every correction for audit.

Access usually follows users.read (or equivalent rules). Cross-check the user profile if you need to verify the account holder.

organisations.title: Organizations
organisations.body:
The [Organizations](/organisations) module lists partners and entities on the platform. Search by name or slug, then open a record to see the profile, contact, and linked employees.

Create an organization with New organization, then complete the details and related settings. Some options (theme, bank accounts) are also managed under [Settings](/parametres).

Access is generally available to authenticated users under RBAC rules; write actions may be restricted.

roles-et-permissions.title: Roles and permissions
roles-et-permissions.summary: Decide who can read or edit each module, with least privilege.
roles-et-permissions.body:
Under [System → Roles](/systeme/roles), define roles and their permissions (read / write per domain). Create a role, select the needed permissions, then assign it to users.

Assignment and permission screens (outside the main menu, reachable via breadcrumb or Ctrl+F search) link a role to a user with a scope (global, property, agency, support queue…).

Least privilege: grant only what is needed. A bad role can hide entire menus or open too much access.

After an assignment, ask the user to sign in again if menus do not refresh. Cross-check [Sessions](/utilisateurs/sessions) & security if you suspect abusive access.

parametres-systeme.title: System settings
parametres-systeme.summary: Emails, donations, public catalog, mobile money, and org settings.
parametres-systeme.body:
The [Settings](/parametres) hub groups organization configuration. From there you can reach transactional emails, donations, mobile money, and bank accounts.

In organization settings, the catalog / enabled products section lets you show or hide each public-site vertical (hotels, flights, car rentals, cruises, activities, packages). A disabled vertical is removed from navigation and returns a not-found page on the public site.

Change settings carefully: a wrong email template, bank account, or accidentally hidden product directly affects customers and operations. Save, then verify a real flow (test payment, notification, public menu).

Typical permissions: organization_settings.read/write, plus specific rights for mobile money or bank accounts. These settings are separate from the [GAP](/gap/parametres) module.

vue-ensemble-tresorerie.title: Treasury overview
vue-ensemble-tresorerie.summary: Hub, monthly indicators, quick links, and display currency.
vue-ensemble-tresorerie.body:
The [Treasury hub](/tresorerie) summarizes the current month's financial activity: total entries, total exits, pending expense requests (submitted or validated), and net balance (entries − exits).

The Quick access block links to the sub-modules you have permission for: [entries](/tresorerie/entrees), [exits](/tresorerie/sorties), [expense requests](/tresorerie/besoins), [budgets](/tresorerie/budgets), [reports](/tresorerie/rapports), [external collaborators](/tresorerie/externes), [audit](/tresorerie/audit), and [accounting](/tresorerie/comptabilite).

Amounts are shown in your organization's default currency, which entry forms also suggest by default — see [Currencies and default currency](/aide/systeme/devises-et-devise-par-defaut).

Base permission: treasury.read. Each sub-module adds its own rights (write, validation, reports, audit); a missing menu usually means a missing permission — see [Roles and permissions](/systeme/roles).

entrees-et-sorties.title: Fund entries and exits
entrees-et-sorties.summary: Record incoming funds, disburse authorized requests, and void an operation.
entrees-et-sorties.body:
[Fund entries](/tresorerie/entrees) record money received: booking payment, direct customer, partner, grant / donation, owner capital, bank interest, or other. Enter the amount, currency, date, and payment method (cash, bank transfer, mobile money, card, cheque), then attach supporting documents. An entry is created with the Recorded status.

[Fund exits](/tresorerie/sorties) always disburse an authorized [expense request](/tresorerie/besoins). An exit moves from Draft to Disbursed, then Recorded; moving to Recorded requires at least one supporting document and closes the linked request.

The default currency is the organization's; only active currencies from the catalog can be selected. If it differs from the exercise's bookkeeping currency, an [exchange rate](/tresorerie/taux-change) is needed to post it to accounting.

A wrong operation is never deleted: use Void with a reason (permission treasury.void). Voiding is logged in the [audit trail](/tresorerie/audit) and refused if the operation is already linked to accounting. Write permissions: treasury.entries.write and treasury.exits.write.

besoins-et-externes.title: Expense requests and external collaborators
besoins-et-externes.summary: Submission, validation, and authorization workflow, plus external access.
besoins-et-externes.body:
An [expense request](/tresorerie/besoins) formalizes a spending request before any disbursement. It follows Draft → Submitted → Validated → Authorized, then becomes Closed when the linked exit is recorded. It can also be Rejected or Cancelled along the way.

Each step needs a separate permission: treasury.expense_requests.create (create, submit), treasury.expense_requests.validate (validate), and treasury.expense_requests.authorize (authorize). Assign these steps to different people to keep a two-person check.

[External collaborators](/tresorerie/externes) (contractors, volunteers, partners) have no admin account. Invite them by email: they receive a secure access link to submit an expense request, which then appears in the admin list. Deactivate an external collaborator as soon as the engagement ends (permission treasury.externals.manage).

budgets-et-suivi.title: Budgets and tracking
budgets-et-suivi.summary: Set monthly or annual envelopes and compare them with actuals.
budgets-et-suivi.body:
[Budgets](/tresorerie/budgets) set an envelope per period (monthly or annual) and per scope: general, activity, or product / service (room, flight class, vehicle, cabin, activity slot…). The currency suggested at creation is the organization's.

[Budget tracking](/tresorerie/budgets/suivi) compares each budget with actuals based on recorded operations. Use it to spot overruns before authorizing new [expense requests](/tresorerie/besoins).

Permissions: treasury.read to view, treasury.budgets.write to create or edit.

taux-de-change.title: Exchange rates
taux-de-change.summary: Enter the manual rates used to post foreign-currency operations.
taux-de-change.body:
The [exchange rates](/tresorerie/taux-change) catalog holds rates entered manually per organization. A rate reads: 1 unit of source currency = rate × target currency (for example 1 EUR = 655.957 XOF). It applies from its effective date.

When creating a rate, the suggested target currency is the organization's and the source currency is EUR (or USD if the organization uses EUR). Only active currencies from the [catalog](/systeme/devises) are available, and source and target must differ.

These rates are used for posting: when an entry or exit is in a currency other than the exercise's bookkeeping currency, the applicable rate is looked up; without a rate, posting is refused. Deleting a rate does not change entries already posted.

Permissions: treasury.fx_rates.read to view, treasury.fx_rates.write to create, edit, or delete.

comptabilite-syscohada.title: SYSCOHADA accounting
comptabilite-syscohada.summary: Treasury-to-entry links, journal, general ledger, trial balance, balance sheet, and income statement.
comptabilite-syscohada.body:
The [Accounting hub](/tresorerie/comptabilite) links each treasury operation to a SYSCOHADA journal entry. Each link is Pending, Linked, or Skipped: Post generates the entry from the mapping rule, Skip excludes the operation from the books.

The [journal](/tresorerie/comptabilite/journal) lists entries (Draft, Posted, Reversed); open one to see its lines, origin, and debit / credit totals. The [general ledger](/tresorerie/comptabilite/grand-livre) details the movements of one account, and the [trial balance](/tresorerie/comptabilite/balance) totals debits, credits, and balances per account; a debit / credit gap points to entries that need checking.

The [balance sheet](/tresorerie/comptabilite/bilan) and the [income statement](/tresorerie/comptabilite/compte-resultat) present the exercise's financial statements. Filter by organization, exercise, and period; amounts are expressed in the exercise's bookkeeping currency.

Permissions: treasury.accounting_link.read or accounting.read for the books, accounting.reports.read for the balance sheet and income statement.

exercices-et-cloture.title: Fiscal years and closing
exercices-et-cloture.summary: Create fiscal years, choose the bookkeeping currency, lock periods, and close.
exercices-et-cloture.body:
[Fiscal years](/tresorerie/comptabilite/exercices) define an organization's accounting period. On creation, monthly periods are generated automatically and the suggested bookkeeping currency is the organization's. It can only be changed while the fiscal year is open and has no posted entries.

The [Closing](/tresorerie/comptabilite/cloture) page lets you lock or unlock each period (Open, Locked, Closed), then close the fiscal year. Closing generates a closing entry and, if a following fiscal year exists, an opening balance carry-forward. This cannot be undone: check the [trial balance](/tresorerie/comptabilite/balance) and the [balance sheet](/tresorerie/comptabilite/bilan) first.

The [accounting audit](/tresorerie/comptabilite/audit) logs actions on entries, fiscal years, and periods (date, action, entity, actor).

Permissions: accounting.chart.write to create a fiscal year, accounting.close to lock and close, accounting.audit.read for the audit.

rapports-et-audit.title: Treasury reports and audit
rapports-et-audit.summary: Period aggregates, breakdown by currency, CSV export, and action log.
rapports-et-audit.body:
[Reports](/tresorerie/rapports) aggregate entries and exits over a period: totals, operation counts, breakdown by source and by payment method. Filter by dates and currency; the net balance is only computed for a single currency, otherwise amounts are shown per currency. Use Export CSV to work on the figures elsewhere.

The [audit log](/tresorerie/audit) records treasury actions: creations, status changes, and voids with their reason. Use it to rebuild the history of an operation or expense request.

Permissions: treasury.reports.read for reports, treasury.audit.read for the log. For the accounting entries audit, see [Fiscal years and closing](/aide/tresorerie-comptabilite/exercices-et-cloture).

devises-et-devise-par-defaut.title: Currencies and default currency
devises-et-devise-par-defaut.summary: Global currency catalog, organization currency, and bookkeeping currency.
devises-et-devise-par-defaut.body:
The [currency catalog](/systeme/devises) lists the ISO codes available across the platform. Only active currencies appear in selectors (amounts, budgets, rates, fiscal years…). Deactivating a currency removes it from lists without changing existing operations, which keep their code. Permissions: currencies.read to view, currencies.write to create or edit.

Each organization has a default currency, chosen from the active currencies. It is used to display amounts in the admin and prefills forms: activities, vehicles, cabins, rooms, employees, bank accounts, treasury operations, budgets, and exchange rates. Change it from the [Organizations](/organisations) record or [Settings](/parametres); the change applies as soon as you save. When no currency is set, the admin uses XOF.

Accounting uses its own bookkeeping currency, set per [fiscal year](/tresorerie/comptabilite/exercices). When an operation is in another currency, an [exchange rate](/tresorerie/taux-change) is required to post it.

Tip: activate a currency in the catalog before assigning it to an organization; a currency outside the active catalog is rejected on save.
